sentences.text: Miogallus was an extinct genus of large pheasants that lived in Europe during the Miocene.
The genus Miogallus contains only one species, Miogallus altus.
Mlíkovský identified Miogallus altus, originally known as Miophasianus altus, after determining the genus Miophasianus was a nomen nudum.
Researchers consider Miogallus longaevus, described by Lambrecht in 1933, to be a likely junior synonym of Miogallus altus.
The species is named Miogallus altus because the genus name Miogallus has priority over Miophasianus.
Miogallus belongs to the family Phasianidae.
The Paleobiology Database classifies Miogallus under the class Reptilia.
The type species for the genus Miogallus is listed as Gallus longaevus.
